<!-- head-1: body_md -->
There exist $p_1,q_1,p_2,q_2>1$, functions $a_1,a_2\in C(\overline\Omega\times[0,\infty))$, and constants
\[
 a_1^*,a_2^*,b_1^*,b_2^*>0
\]
such that $a_i(x,t)\ge a_i^*>0$ and
\begin{align}
F\bigl(x,t,u,v,V(t)\bigr)
&\ge a_1(x,t)v^{p_1}+b_1^*V(t)^{p_2},\label{eq:A1F}\\
G\bigl(x,t,u,v,U(t)\bigr)
&\ge a_2(x,t)u^{q_1}+b_2^*U(t)^{q_2}.\label{eq:A1G}
\end{align}
<!-- end head-1 -->
<!-- head-2: body_md -->
For some $\alpha,\beta>1$, $0<\rho,\sigma<1$, positive constants $c_1,c_2,C_1,C_2$, nonnegative constants $b_1,b_2$, and bounded nonnegative functions $A_1,A_2$ satisfying
\[
 0\le A_1(x,t)\le A_1^*,\qquad 0\le A_2(x,t)\le A_2^*,
\]
assume $0<c_i\le C_i$ and
\begin{align}
 c_1V(t)^\alpha
 &\le F\bigl(x,t,u,v,V(t)\bigr)
 \le C_1V(t)^\alpha+A_1(x,t)v^\rho+b_1,\label{eq:A2F}\\
 c_2U(t)^\beta
 &\le G\bigl(x,t,u,v,U(t)\bigr)
 \le C_2U(t)^\beta+A_2(x,t)u^\sigma+b_2.\label{eq:A2G}
\end{align}
<!-- end head-2 -->
<!-- head-3: body_md -->
A classical solution to (\ref{eq:system}) on $[0,T)$ means a pair $(u,v)$ with
\[
 u,v\in C(\overline\Omega\times[0,T))\cap C^{2,1}(\Omega\times(0,T))
\]
which satisfies the governing equations in $\Omega\times(0,T)$, as well as the compatible boundary conditions for $0<t<T$ and the initial data continuously at $t=0$.
<!-- end head-3 -->
<!-- proposition-1: body_md -->
\label{prop:local}
Assume H1--H4. Then \eqref{eq:system} has a unique nonnegative classical solution $(u,v)$ on a maximal interval
\[
 [0,T_{\max}),\qquad 0<T_{\max}\le\infty.
\]
If $T_{\max}<\infty$, then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:cont}
 \limsup_{t\uparrowT_{\max}}
 \left(\left\lVert u(\cdot,t)\right\rVert_{L^\infty(\Omega)}+
 \left\lVert v(\cdot,t)\right\rVert_{L^\infty(\Omega)}\right)=\infty.
\end{equation}
<!-- end proposition-1 -->
<!-- proof-1: body_md -->
The Dirichlet and Neumann Laplacians generate analytic positive heat semigroups on $C(\overline\Omega)$.
 Since $w\mapsto\int_\Omega w$ is a bounded linear functional on $C(\overline\Omega)$, the induced nonlocal reaction map is locally Lipschitz on bounded subsets of $C(\overline\Omega)^2$.
Combining it with H1-H4,  we can use standard semilinear parabolic theory to obtain local existence, uniqueness, and the blowup alternative, see \cite{Henry1981,Amann1984}.  As a result, the only obstruction to continuation at finite time is unboundedness of the $C(\overline\Omega)^2$ norm, which is exactly \eqref{eq:cont}.
<!-- end proof-1 -->
<!-- head-4: body_md -->
When $T_{\max}<\infty$, we call $T_{\max}$ the blow-up time.  Especially, if there exists a finite time $T$ such that
\[
 \lim_{t\uparrow T}\bigl(U(t)+V(t)\bigr)=\infty,
\]
we say that the solution undergoes $L^1$ blow-up at time $T$.
<!-- end head-4 -->
<!-- lemma-1: body_md -->
\label{lem:min}
Let
\[
 P(y)=\sum_{i=1}^m a_i y^{\tilde{p}_i},\qquad
 Q(x)=\sum_{j=1}^n b_j z^{\tilde{q}_j},
\]
where $a_i,b_j>0$ and $\tilde{p}_i,\tilde{q}_j>1$. Define
\begin{equation}\label{eq:hdef}
 h(s)=\min_{0\le z\le s}\{P(s-z)+Q(z)\},\qquad s\ge0.
\end{equation}
Then:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textnormal{(\roman*)}]
\item the minimum is attained for every $s\ge0$;
\item $h(0)=0$, $h(s)>0$ for $s>0$, and $h$ is continuous and locally Lipschitz on $[0,\infty)$;
\item $h(s)/s$ is nondecreasing on $(0,\infty)$;
\item there exist $c>0$, $r>1$, and $s_*>0$ such that $h(s)\ge cs^r$ for $s\ge s_*$.
\end{enumerate}
Consequently,
\[
 \int_R^\infty \frac{\,\mathrm{d} s}{h(s)}<\infty
\]
for every $R>0$.
<!-- end lemma-1 -->
<!-- head-5: body_md -->
Note that for fixed $s$, the objective in \eqref{eq:hdef} is continuous on the compact interval $[0,s]$, so the minimum value can be attained and it can vanish only at $s=0$.

Let $z=\theta s$ and 
\[
 \mathcal F(s,\theta)=P((1-\theta)s)+Q(\theta s),
 \qquad (s,\theta)\in[0,\infty)\times[0,1].
\]
Then $h(s)=\min_{0\le\theta\le1}\mathcal F(s,\theta)$ and $h$ is continuous because uniform continuity of $\mathcal F$ on compact rectangles. Moreover, the family $\{\mathcal F(\cdot,\theta)\}_{\theta\in[0,1]}$ is equi-Lipschitz on each $[0,R]\times[0,1]$ because the $s$-derivatives of all monomial terms are uniformly bounded. As a result, $h(s)$ preserves the same Lipschitz bound.

For $s>0$, let
\[
 \frac{h(s)}s
 =\min_{0\le\theta\le1}
 \left[
 \sum_i a_i(1-\theta)^{\tilde{p}_i}s^{\tilde{p}_i-1}
 +\sum_j b_j\theta^{\tilde{q}_j}s^{\tilde{q}_j-1}
 \right].
\]
Since all exponents $\tilde{p}_i-1$ and $\tilde{q}_j-1$ are positive, the bracket is nondecreasing in $s$ for each fixed $\theta$. Consequently, its minimum is nondecreasing.

Denote $p_0=p_{i_0}$, $a_0=a_{i_0}$, $q=q_{j_0}$ and $b=b_{j_0}$ for arbitrarily chosen $i_0$ and $j_0$. Since for every $z\in[0,s]$, either $s-z\ge s/2$ or $z\ge s/2$, we have
\[
 P(s-z)+Q(z)\ge \min\{a2^{-p}s^p,b2^{-q}s^q\}.
\]
Especially, this is bounded below by $cs^r$ for $s\ge1$ with
\[
 r=\min\{p,q\}>1,
 \qquad c=\min\{a2^{-p},b2^{-q}\}>0.
\]
(iv) is proved and the Osgood integrability follows.\hfill $\Box$
<!-- end head-5 -->
<!-- lemma-2: body_md -->
\label{lem:osgood}
 Assume that $S:[0,T)\to(0,\infty)$ is a locally absolutely continuous satisfies 
\begin{equation}\label{eq:osgdiff}
 S'(t)\ge-\lambda S(t)+h(S(t))\quad\text{for a.e. }t\in(0,T),
 \qquad S(0)=S_0>0.
\end{equation}
Here $h$ is defined in Lemma~\ref{lem:min} and $\lambda\ge 0$ is a constant. If
\begin{equation}\label{eq:thresholdabstract}
 h(S_0)>\lambda S_0,
\end{equation}
then $S(t)\ge S_0$ and
\begin{equation}\label{eq:osgbound}
 T\le \int_{S_0}^{\infty}\frac{\,\mathrm{d} s}{h(s)-\lambda s}.
\end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-2 -->
<!-- head-6: body_md -->
Since $h(s)/s$ is nondecreasing,
\[
 \frac{h(s)-\lambda s}{s}
 \ge \frac{h(S_0)}{S_0}-\lambda=:\delta>0,
 \qquad s\ge S_0.
\]
Substituting it into (\ref{eq:osgdiff}),  we can  $S'\ge\delta S_0>0$ almost everywhere. 

Let $g(s)=h(s)-\lambda s>0$ for $s\ge S_0$ and
\[
 \Psi(r)=\int_{S_0}^{r}\frac{\,\mathrm{d} s}{g(s)}.
\]
 By Lemma~\ref{lem:min}, $h(s)\ge cs^r$ with $r>1$ for large $s$, hence $g(s)\ge(c/2)s^r$ eventually, and $\Psi(\infty)<\infty$.

Using the chain rule for absolutely continuous functions, we obtain
\[
 \frac{\,\mathrm{d}}{\,\mathrm{d} t}\Psi(S(t))=\frac{S'(t)}{g(S(t))}\ge 1
\]
for almost every $t$. Integrating it, we obtain  $t\le\Psi(S(t))\le\Psi(\infty)<\infty$ for all $t<T$, and \eqref{eq:osgbound} as $t\uparrow T$.\hfill $\Box$
<!-- end head-6 -->
<!-- lemma-3: body_md -->
\label{lem:diridentity}
Under the Dirichlet boundary condition, we have
\begin{align}
 X'(t)&=-\lambda_1X(t)+\int_\Omega F(t)\varphi_1\,\mathrm{d} x,\label{eq:Xprime}\\
 Y'(t)&=-\lambda_1Y(t)+\int_\Omega G(t)\varphi_1\,\mathrm{d} x.\label{eq:Yprime}
\end{align}
<!-- end lemma-3 -->
<!-- head-7: body_md -->
Let $S_D(t)$ be the Dirichlet heat semigroup. By Duhamel's formula, we get
\[
 u(t)=S_D(t-s)u(s)+\int_s^t S_D(t-\tau)F(\tau)\,\mathrm{d}\tau
\]
for $0\le s<t<T_{\max}$. 
The semigroup is self-adjoint on $L^2(\Omega)$ and $S_D(t)\varphi_1=e^{-\lambda_1 t}\varphi_1$. Therefore,
\[
 X(t)=e^{-\lambda_1(t-s)}X(s)
 +\int_s^t e^{-\lambda_1(t-\tau)}
 \left(\int_\Omega F(\tau)\varphi_1\,\mathrm{d} x\right)\,\mathrm{d}\tau,
\]
which implies \eqref{eq:Xprime}. \eqref{eq:Yprime} can  be obtained similarly.  \hfill $\Box$
<!-- end head-7 -->
<!-- theorem-1: body_md -->
\label{thm:abstractD}
Suppose that nonnegative moments $X,Y$ satisfy
\[
 X'\ge-\lambda X+P(Y),\qquad
 Y'\ge-\lambda Y+Q(X),
\]
where $\lambda>0$ and $P,Q$ are defined in Lemma~\ref{lem:min}. 
If $h(S_0)>\lambda S_0$, then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:abstractDbound}
 T_{\max}\le \int_{S_0}^\infty\frac{\,\mathrm{d} s}{h(s)-\lambda s},
\end{equation}
where $h(s)$ is defined by (\ref{eq:hdef}).
<!-- end theorem-1 -->
<!-- head-8: body_md -->
Adding the two inequalities, we get
\[
 S'\ge-\lambda S+P(Y)+Q(X)\ge-\lambda S+h(S).
\]
Using Lemma~\ref{lem:osgood}, we get the conclusion.\hfill $\Box$
<!-- end head-8 -->
<!-- theorem-2: body_md -->
\label{thm:A1N}
Assume that H1--H4 hold. Then under Assumption 1 and homogeneous Neumann boundary conditions,  for every nonzero nonnegative initial datum, the solution has finite maximal existence time and
\begin{equation}\label{eq:A1Nbound}
 T_{\max}\le\int_{W_0}^{\infty}\frac{\,\mathrm{d} s}{h_{1,N}(s)},
 \qquad W_0=U(0)+V(0)>0.
\end{equation}
<!-- end theorem-2 -->
<!-- head-9: body_md -->
Using \eqref{eq:A1NU}--\eqref{eq:A1NV}, we obtain
\[
 W'\ge P_{1,N}(V)+Q_{1,N}(U)\ge h_{1,N}(W).
\]
Since $W_0>0$, by the results of  Lemmas~\ref{lem:min} and Lemmas~\ref{lem:osgood} with $\lambda=0$,  $W$ cannot remain finite beyond the right-hand side of \eqref{eq:A1Nbound}. That is, every classical solution has finite mass before its maximal time $T_{\max}$ which is bounded by the finite integral in \eqref{eq:A1Nbound}.
\hfill $\Box$
<!-- end head-9 -->
<!-- theorem-3: body_md -->
\label{thm:A1D}
Assume thatH1--H4 hold. Then under Assumption 1 and homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions,  for every nonzero nonnegative initial datum, the solution has finite maximal existence time. If
\begin{equation}\label{eq:A1Dthreshold}
 h_{1,D}(S_0)>\lambda_1S_0,
\end{equation}
then $T_{\max}<\infty$ and
\begin{equation}\label{eq:A1Dbound}
 T_{\max}\le\int_{S_0}^{\infty}
 \frac{\,\mathrm{d} s}{h_{1,D}(s)-\lambda_1s}.
\end{equation}
<!-- end theorem-3 -->
<!-- head-10: body_md -->
Applying Theorem~\ref{thm:abstractD} to the two weighted-moment inequalities above, we can obtian the conclusion.
\hfill $\Box$
<!-- end head-10 -->
<!-- theorem-4: body_md -->
\label{thm:A2N}
Assume that H1--H4 hold. Then under Assumption 2 and homogeneous Neumann boundary conditions, for every nonzero nonnegative initial datum, the solution has finite maximal existence time and
\begin{equation}\label{eq:A2Nbound}
 T_{\max}\le\int_{W_0}^{\infty}\frac{\,\mathrm{d} s}{h_{2,N}(s)}.
\end{equation}
<!-- end theorem-4 -->
<!-- head-11: body_md -->
Since $W'\ge h_{2,N}(W)$ and $W_0>0$, using Lemmas~\ref{lem:min} and \ref{lem:osgood}, we can get \eqref{eq:A2Nbound}. 
\hfill $\Box$
<!-- end head-11 -->
<!-- theorem-5: body_md -->
\label{thm:A2D}
Assume that H1--H4 hold. Then under Assumption 2 and homogeneous Neumann boundary conditions, for every nonzero nonnegative initial datum, the solution has finite maximal existence time. If
\begin{equation}\label{eq:A2Dthreshold}
 h_{2,D}(S_0)>\lambda_1S_0,
\end{equation}
then $T_{\max}<\infty$ and
\begin{equation}\label{eq:A2Dbound}
 T_{\max}\le\int_{S_0}^{\infty}
 \frac{\,\mathrm{d} s}{h_{2,D}(s)-\lambda_1s}.
\end{equation}
<!-- end theorem-5 -->
<!-- head-12: body_md -->
Applying Theorem~\ref{thm:abstractD}, we can obtain the conclusion.
\hfill $\Box$
<!-- end head-12 -->
<!-- lemma-4: body_md -->
\label{lem:eqmin}
Let $A,B>0$ and $r>1$. Then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:eqmin}
 \min_{0\le z\le s}\{A(s-z)^r+Bz^r\}
 =\left(A^{-1/(r-1)}+B^{-1/(r-1)}\right)^{-(r-1)}s^r.
\end{equation}
For $s>0$ the minimizer is unique and satisfies
\[
 Bz^{r-1}=A(s-z)^{r-1}.
\]
<!-- end lemma-4 -->
<!-- head-13: body_md -->
By strict convexity, there exists a unique critical point. Let $a=A^{-1/(r-1)}$ and $b=B^{-1/(r-1)}$. The critical-point relation yields
\[
 s-z=\frac{a}{a+b}s,\qquad z=\frac{b}{a+b}s.
\]
Substituting them into (\ref{eq:eqmin}), we get the conclusion.\hfill $\Box$
<!-- end head-13 -->
<!-- corollary-1: body_md -->
\label{cor:eq}
Assume that $\alpha=\beta=r>1$ and define
\begin{equation}\label{eq:CN}
 C_N=\left(c_1^{-1/(r-1)}+c_2^{-1/(r-1)}\right)^{-(r-1)}.
\end{equation}
Then under homogeneous Neumann boundary conditions,
\[
 h_{2,N}(s)=DC_Ns^r,
\]
and
\begin{equation}\label{eq:eqNbound}
 T_{\max}\le\frac{W_0^{1-r}}{(r-1)DC_N}.
\end{equation}
Under homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions, let
\begin{equation}\label{eq:CD}
 C_D=M_{\varphi}^{-r}C_N.
\end{equation}
If
\begin{equation}\label{eq:eqDthreshold}
 C_DS_0^{r-1}>\lambda_1,
\end{equation}
then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:eqDbound}
 T_{\max}\le
 \frac{1}{(r-1)\lambda_1}
 \log\!\left(
 \frac{C_DS_0^{r-1}}{C_DS_0^{r-1}-\lambda_1}
 \right).
\end{equation}
<!-- end corollary-1 -->
<!-- head-14: body_md -->
Since the definitions of $h_{2,N}$ and $h_{2,D}$ have been defined in Lemma~\ref{lem:eqmin}. The Neumann integral is elementary. In the Dirichlet case,
\[
 \int_{S_0}^{\infty}\frac{\,\mathrm{d} s}{C_Ds^r-\lambda_1s}
 =\frac{1}{(r-1)\lambda_1}
 \log\!\left(
 \frac{C_DS_0^{r-1}}{C_DS_0^{r-1}-\lambda_1}
 \right),
\]
provided \eqref{eq:eqDthreshold} holds.
\hfill $\Box$
<!-- end head-14 -->
<!-- theorem-6: body_md -->
\label{thm:lowerLinf}
Assume that H1--H4 hold. Then under Assumption 2, with either homogeneous Dirichlet or homogeneous Neumann boundary conditions,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:lowerLinf}
 T_{\max}\ge\int_{Z_0}^{\infty}\frac{\,\mathrm{d} s}{H_\infty(s)},
 \qquad
 Z_0=\left\lVert u_0\right\rVert_\infty+\left\lVert v_0\right\rVert_\infty>0.
\end{equation}
<!-- end theorem-6 -->
<!-- head-15: body_md -->
Let $z$ solve
\[
 z'=H_\infty(z),\qquad z(0)=Z_0.
\]
Note that the function $H_\infty$ is continuous, locally Lipschitz, positive, and nondecreasing on $[0,\infty)$. Applying the standard Dini-derivative comparison to \eqref{eq:ZDini}, we get that $Z(t)\le z(t)$ while both are finite. The scalar blowup time of $z$ is
\[
 \tau_\infty=\int_{Z_0}^{\infty}\frac{\,\mathrm{d} s}{H_\infty(s)},
\]
which is finite because $\alpha,\beta>1$. If $T_{\max}<\tau_\infty$, then $Z(t)$ would remain bounded as $t\uparrowT_{\max}$, contradicting the continuation criterion \eqref{eq:cont}. Hence \eqref{eq:lowerLinf} holds.
\hfill $\Box$
<!-- end head-15 -->
<!-- proposition-2: body_md -->
\label{prop:l1lower}
Assume that H1--H4 hold.  Under Assumption 2, with either homogeneous Dirichlet or homogeneous Neumann boundary conditions, if the maximal solution undergoes $L^1$ blow-up at a finite time $T$, then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:l1lower}
 T\ge\int_{W_0}^{\infty}\frac{\,\mathrm{d} s}{H_1(s)}.
\end{equation}
<!-- end proposition-2 -->
<!-- head-16: body_md -->
Let $w$ solve $w'=H_1(w)$, $w(0)=W_0$. Using Dini's comparison principle, we get $W(t)\le w(t)$ when $w$ is finite. The scalar blowup time is bounded by the right-hand side of \eqref{eq:l1lower}. 
\hfill $\Box$
<!-- end head-16 -->
<!-- corollary-2: body_md -->
\label{cor:twosided}
Assume H1--H4 and Assumption 2 hold. 
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textnormal{(\roman*)}]
\item Under homogeneous Neumann boundary conditions,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:twosidedN}
 \int_{Z_0}^{\infty}\frac{\,\mathrm{d} s}{H_\infty(s)}
 \le T_{\max}
 \le \int_{W_0}^{\infty}\frac{\,\mathrm{d} s}{h_{2,N}(s)}.
\end{equation}
\item Under homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions, if $h_{2,D}(S_0)>\lambda_1S_0$, then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:twosidedD}
 \int_{Z_0}^{\infty}\frac{\,\mathrm{d} s}{H_\infty(s)}
 \le T_{\max}
 \le \int_{S_0}^{\infty}\frac{\,\mathrm{d} s}{h_{2,D}(s)-\lambda_1s}.
\end{equation}
\end{enumerate}
If, in addition, $L^1$ blow-up occurs at the maximal time, Proposition~\ref{prop:l1lower} supplies the further lower bound \eqref{eq:l1lower}.
<!-- end corollary-2 -->
<!-- proposition-3: body_md -->
\label{prop:noLowerA1}
Fixing a domain, exponents, the coefficients in Assumption 1 and a positive constant initial datum for the Neumann problem, then there is no positive lower bound for $T_{\max}$ that depends only on these data and is valid for every reaction pair satisfying Assumption 1.
<!-- end proposition-3 -->
<!-- head-17: body_md -->
If we take $u_0=v_0=m>0$, fix $r>1$ and set
\begin{align*}
 F_K&=a_1^*v^{p_1}+b_1^*V^{p_2}+Ku^r,\\
 G_K&=a_2^*u^{q_1}+b_2^*U^{q_2}+Kv^r
\end{align*} 
for every $K>0$, then these reactions satisfy Assumption 1. And we have
\[
 u'(t)\ge Ku(t)^r,
\]
consequently,
\[
 T_{\max}^{(K)}\le\frac{m^{1-r}}{(r-1)K}\longrightarrow0
 \qquad(K\to\infty).
\]
Thus no positive lower bound can depend only on the Assumption  1 with lower-growth data and this fixed initial datum.

Similarly, in the case of Dirichlet boundary condition, adding $Ku^r$ and testing against $\varphi_1$, one can obtain $X'\ge-\lambda_1X+KX^r$, whose Osgood upper time tends to zero as $K\to\infty$ once $KX_0^{r-1}>\lambda_1$. \hfill $\Box$
<!-- end head-17 -->
